task: Restore Tornado WebSocket TCP_NODELAY delegation after stream ownership moved behind the protocol

subtasks.description: Detect a green-suite false positive by checking the real public delegation path
lessons: A proxy repair can pass the existing suite while targeting the wrong public surface; the contract test must begin at the caller named in the issue.

subtasks.description: Route WebSocketHandler set_nodelay through the protocol to the active stream
lessons: When resource ownership moves behind an abstraction, public controls must follow the ownership chain instead of retaining a stale direct reference.

constraints: CPython 3.7 was unavailable on macOS arm64; the complete suite used isolated CPython 3.8.20 with a temporary cancellation-only compatibility shim that was removed after testing.
The first frozen candidate targeted the wrong client surface and was rejected after evaluator comparison; the successful second attempt was therefore evaluator-informed.
No raw logs, prompts, source patches, credentials, or private workspace paths are published.
lessons: Trace delegation from the issue's public entry point through every ownership boundary before choosing where to add a proxy.
A full green legacy suite cannot validate behavior that has no regression test; add a focused contract test that asserts the exact delegate call.
Reject a green patch when evaluator comparison proves that it repaired a plausible but different API surface.
Keep runtime-compatibility shims separate from the candidate patch and recheck the candidate hash after removing them.
